description: Build a local pre-flight validator that runs BEFORE any RunPod pod is spun up for training. Reads /home/workspace/shared/sft/RUNPOD_PRECONDITIONS.md (especially section #7 'Pre-Flight Crash') as the contract. Input: path to a JSONL training corpus (default /home/workspace/shared/sft/data/train.jsonl). Three checks, all must pass for exit 0; any failure prints actionable error and exits non-zero before a single API call: (1) SCHEMA — every row parses as JSON, has 'messages' list with at least system+user+assistant roles, all 'content' fields are strings, no nulls. Print row index of first failure. (2) TOKENIZER SIMULATION — load the Qwen2.5 tokenizer via transformers.AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('Qwen/Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct') with trust_remote_code=True; for every example, render via apply_chat_template(tokenize=False) then tokenize and check len <= MAX_SEQ_LEN (default 2048). Report distribution: count of examples in each quartile of token length, plus count exceeding the cap. Fail if any single example exceeds cap OR if 95th-percentile is >85% of cap (= corpus is straining packer). (3) VRAM ESTIMATE — given target_gpu_gb (default 24) and base model param count (default 3.09B for Qwen2.5-3B), compute: weights_bf16 = params * 2 bytes; optimiser_8bit = params * 2 bytes; gradients_bf16 = params * 2 bytes (only on LoRA params actually, ~0.5% of base); activations = batch * max_seq * hidden_size * 4 bytes (Qwen2.5-3B hidden_size=2048). Target headroom: 15%. Fail if estimate > target_gpu_gb * 0.85. Print the breakdown either way. CLI: python3 sft_dataset_preflight.py --jsonl PATH [--max-seq-len N] [--gpu-gb N] [--base-model NAME]. NO API calls anywhere — this runs entirely on ZoComputer. NO duckdb writes — results print to stdout AND write to /home/workspace/shared/sft/preflight_report.json (atomic temp+rename). FileHandler logging only to /home/workspace/logs/sft_dataset_preflight.log. Idempotent: re-running on the same JSONL produces the same report. Closes RUNPOD_PRECONDITIONS.md gotcha #7 — catches malformed JSONL, length blow-outs, and VRAM overflow before a pod is billed for them.
